brief.headline: Memory bear market: Samsung/Hynix drop 9-14% on profit-taking; HBM3E pricing slides as Q3 contract forecasts decelerate
brief.summary: <cite index="18-8,18-10">Samsung fell 9.06% to ₩286,000 and SK Hynix dropped 14.57% to ₩2,187,000 Thursday</cite> as global tech selloff spilled into Korea. <cite index="21-7,21-9">Both stocks plus Micron and the Roundhill Memory ETF are now down >20% from recent highs despite Samsung's monster Q2 profit estimates of $59B operating income and $113B revenue</cite>. <cite index="4-1,4-14">HBM3E contract pricing is ~$13-17/GB as of early 2026, down from H1 2025 peak of $17-20/GB</cite>, while <cite index="12-1">conventional DRAM contract prices are forecast to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND 10-15%—a marked deceleration from Q1's 90-95% spike</cite>. <cite index="37-10">CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from 20% currently to 10% by end-2026</cite>. SK Hynix closed <cite index="19-9,19-10">Friday US debut up 13% at $168 after raising $26.5B, the largest foreign IPO in US history</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Short Samsung vs. long SK Hynix into Q3. Hynix holds structural edge: <cite index="1-9,2-3,2-19">SK Hynix leads HBM with 50-55% market share vs. Samsung's 35-40%</cite>, and <cite index="4-3,4-16">SK Hynix commands premium pricing while Samsung discounts ~30% below Hynix to win design slots</cite>. <cite index="18-14,18-15,18-16">Hynix announced ₩100T ($64.4B) investment with M17 NAND fab starting construction in 2027 and P&T7 packaging expansion to meet HBM server and eSSD demand</cite>. Samsung's blowout Q2 print triggered profit-taking not fresh upside; Hynix's Nasdaq dual-listing adds US demand cushion. <cite index="20-1,20-2">Commerce Secretary Lutnick pressing both to expand US memory production, but Hynix already building $4B Indiana advanced packaging facility for 2028 completion</cite>. HBM mix rotation favors Hynix: <cite index="7-15,7-16">2026 revenue mix forecast at 55% HBM4 / 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 ramping Q3 to absorb HBM3E demand</cite>, playing to Hynix's first-mover advantage on next-gen stacks.

memory_cycle.stage: Late expansion, decelerating into early plateau
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-10,11-11">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026—buyers paid roughly double vs. Q4 2025</cite>. <cite index="12-1">Q3 2026 forecast is 13-18% DRAM, 10-15% NAND—still rising but parabolic phase maturing</cite>. <cite index="11-26,11-27">First genuine strain signal is behavioral: buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes, NAND spot trading gone quiet, though headline numbers stay green—defensible read is parabolic phase maturing, not that peak has arrived</cite>. <cite index="8-1,8-14">ASP gap between HBM3E and DDR5 expected to narrow significantly in 2026; HBM investment tightening supply-demand balance for standard DRAM</cite>. Consumer destruction real—<cite index="53-2,53-3">Gartner projects PC shipments down 10.4%, smartphones down 8.4% in 2026; PC prices up 17%, smartphone prices up 13% vs. 2025</cite>—but enterprise pull hasn't flinched.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-8">HBM3 costs ~$200/24GB stack, HBM3E ~$300/36GB stack, HBM4 ~$500/48GB stack as of July 2026</cite>. <cite index="4-1,4-14">HBM3E contract pricing ~$13-17/GB early 2026, down from $17-20/GB peak in H1 2025</cite>—pricing softening on dual-sourcing gains and <cite index="7-2,7-7">HBM3E was expected to ease as HBM4 enters market, but ongoing H200/ASIC launches by global big tech are keeping demand on steady growth path</cite>. <cite index="1-14">Supply remains constrained through 2026; lead times for HBM3E stacks at 20-26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="7-3,7-8">H200 China export approval pushed HBM3E demand beyond expectations—each H200 incorporates 6 stacks of HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="7-11,7-13">Google TPU and Amazon Trainium shipments begin 2026 with 8 HBM3E stacks/chip (Google) and 4 stacks (Trainium3)</cite>. <cite index="13-11">HBM4 launches Q3 2026</cite>; watch for qualification timing at Nvidia/AMD/hyperscaler ASICs. Margin spread compressing but absolute dollars still extraordinary.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 9-14% as memory stocks enter bear market despite blowout Samsung Q2 profit
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after epic run; Samsung Q2 op profit ₩89.4T ($58.4B, +19x YoY) beat consensus but failed to impress. Memory complex down >20% from June highs—MU, Samsung, Hynix, DRAM ETF all in bear. Sentiment inflection risk: market questioning how much good news already priced.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix raises $26.5B in largest foreign US IPO, closes +13% Friday; Lutnick urges US fab expansion
news_pulse.implication: 177.9M ADRs priced at $149, topped Alibaba's 2014 record. Demand 7x oversubscribed. Commerce Secretary in talks with Samsung/Hynix on US memory production; Micron commits $250B domestic investment. Geopolitical diversification theme gaining traction—watch for CHIPS Act allocation announcements.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 2026 memory price growth decelerates: DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% vs. Q1's 90-95% spike
news_pulse.implication: Slowdown from record Q1 pace signals cycle maturation. AI server demand still supporting prices but consumer destruction mounting—PC DRAM supply shrinking as capacity reallocates to server. Enterprise SSD supply constrained by internal DRAM shortages. High base effects taking hold.

news_pulse.headline: HBM3E contract pricing $13-17/GB early 2026, down from $17-20/GB H1 2025 peak; Samsung discounts 30% vs. Hynix
news_pulse.implication: Pricing compression as Samsung and Micron ramp qualification. Samsung trading margin for share—30% discount to win design slots. Hyperscaler dual-sourcing pressure rising. HBM4 launch Q3 2026 will reset ASP structure; watch qualification announcements for B200/MI325X/TPU v6.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex consensus: $602-725B, up 36-77% YoY; ~75% AI infrastructure, $450B+ AI-specific
news_pulse.implication: Amazon ~$200B, MSFT ~$190B, Google $175-185B, Meta $125-145B (raised from $115-135B). Bullish for memory/storage demand through 2027, but capex-to-revenue gap widening—markets repricing ROI risk. Meta guidance raise cited higher component pricing and data center costs.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; capacity 115-140K wpm, 170K in 2027
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS expanding at 80% CAGR 2022-2027; bottleneck easing supports Nvidia Blackwell/Rubin ramp and AMD MI325X/MI350. Nvidia still holds majority allocation. CoPoS pilot production mid-2027, mass production 2028-2029 for next-gen ASIC integration. Removes key constraint on AI accelerator shipments.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix CEO: ₩100T ($64B) investment—₩80T for M17 NAND fab (ops H1 2029), ₩20T for P&T7 advanced packaging
news_pulse.implication: M17 NAND fab in Chungcheong region targets enterprise SSD surge. P&T7 packaging expansion supports HBM4/HBM4E assembly. Investment accelerates Hynix's vertical integration vs. Samsung. Construction begins 2027; implies Hynix expecting sustained AI infrastructure demand into 2029-2030.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM spot prices still rising into early June 2026 but buyers no longer chasing higher quotes—behavioral strain emerging
news_pulse.implication: First genuine cycle strain signal: buyers pulling back even as contract prices climb. NAND spot trading gone quiet. Retail PC/smartphone demand destruction offsetting enterprise strength. Parabolic phase maturing—defensible read is moderation, not peak, but momentum slowing. Watch Q3 contract negotiations for price resistance.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI vols elevated; Samsung/Hynix drawdown dragging index (both now ~50% of KOSPI weight vs. 25% at end-2025). ADR-KRX arb compressed on Hynix debut—monitor SKHYV vs. 000660.KS spread for dual-listing flow. Memory ETF (DRAM) -7% premarket Wednesday, now -20%+ from June highs. Skew turning bearish; recommend fade rallies into Q3 earnings (Samsung late-July, Hynix early-Aug). Put spreads on Samsung Aug/Sep attractive if IV stays elevated. CoWoS bottleneck easing into year-end is medium-term NVDA call catalyst but near-term memory complex over-owned.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung Q2 detailed earnings release (preliminary was revenue ₩171T, op profit ₩89.4T)—watch HBM revenue mix, foundry utilization, and Q3 capex guidance
SK Hynix US trading Monday open (ticker change SKHYV → SKHY)—monitor ADR arbitrage vs. Korea, institutional accumulation signals
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price updates for DDR5/HBM3E—July 10-11 data would show if behavioral pullback translating to price
Hyperscaler earnings/commentary (if any): Microsoft FY Q4 (mid-July), Google Q2 (late-July)—capex revisions and memory procurement color
CoWoS capacity commentary from TSMC supply-chain checks or July 18 earnings call—confirmation of 115-140K wpm end-2026 target
